candidates.title: fragments
candidates.text:
# Working with fragments

Reruns are a central part of every Streamlit app. When users interact with widgets, your script reruns from top to bottom, and your app's frontend is updated. Streamlit provides several features to help you develop your app within this execution model. Streamlit version 1.37.0 introduced fragments to allow rerunning a portion of your code instead of your full script. As your app grows larger and more complex, these fragment reruns help your app be efficient and performant. Fragments give you finer, easy-to-understand control over your app's execution flow.

Before you read about fragments, we recommend having a basic understanding of [caching](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching), [Session State](/concepts/architecture/session-state), and [forms](/develop/concepts/architecture/forms).

candidates.title: Fragment to fragment (co-fragment) communication instead of rerunning entire app
candidates.text:
### How?

My app looks like the below:

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

The black outlines are fragments. The purple/pink outlines are nested fragments. I understand co-fragment communication occurs through session_state which is great but for this communication to be recognised, one must re-run the whole app. This makes the app more slow and somewhat buggy in my experience of operating my app. 

Seeing as fragments can be re-run periodically, it would be great to add the possibility to communicate between specific fragments via an action. For example, in my app image, After I input details in the "Contact Details" expander, I want to update the CV Preview fragment. But to do that, I have to re-run the entire app. Perhaps the possibility to rerun specific fragments based on some unique Id (like a key of a streamlit widget) when I say click on the submit form button in the Contact Details expander would be great. 

Just an example
```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"])
```

The issue with the above is for every rerun action, the `keys to update` will rerun. So perhaps, we could create a trigger command parameter.

```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=["form_submit_btn"])
```

We could also get fancy and connect trigger keys to keys to update:


```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=[{"frag1":"form_submit_btn"}])
```

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.0
- Python version: 3.13.2
- Operating System: MasOS 15.1
- Browser: Safari, Chrome, and Brave

- 🎯 Introducing event-scoped fragment reruns, which let a widget callback rerun just one named fragment:
    - Name a fragment with `@st.fragment(key=…)` and target it with [`st.rerun`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.rerun)`("filters")` or `st.rerun(["alpha", "beta"])` from an `on_change` or `on_click` callback ([#16161](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16161)).
    - `st.rerun()` and `st.switch_page()` now take effect inside widget callbacks instead of being discarded with a warning; apps that relied on the previous no-op will now rerun ([#16158](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16158)).
- ✨ Introducing `on_change="ignore"`, a new mode that updates a widget in the browser without rerunning your app. Your script receives the buffered value on the next rerun, such as a button click, and the mode is available on [`st.slider`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.slider) and [`st.text_input`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.text_input) ([#14828](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14828), [#16605](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16605)).
- 🍿 Introducing `type="step"`

candidates.text:
### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment()
def toggle_and_text():
    if st.button("rerun"):
        st.rerun()
    t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo', key='t')
    st.info(f't = {t}')

toggle_and_text()
st.header('Outside Fragment')
st.info(f'session_state_t = {st.session_state.t}')
st.button("Update")
```

Streamlit apps directly with `python app.py` or `uv run app.py` using the new `App.run()` entry point — no more `streamlit run` required ([#15563](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15563), [#9450](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9450), [#11420](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11420)).
- 🧩 [`st.fragment`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.fragment) can now write to containers defined outside the fragment. Fragments can update any part of your app — including elements created before the fragment — without triggering a full rerun ([#15623](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15623), [#15620](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15620), [#10481](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10481)).

- 🎛 [`st.chat_input`](/develop/api-reference/chat/st.chat_input) has a new `submit_mode` parameter that controls widget behavior after the user submits a message, e.g. showing a stop button or disabling the chat input ([#14344](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14344), [#8323](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8323), [#11854](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11854)).

- 🔗 [`st.markdown`](/develop/api-reference/text/st.markdown) has a new `anchors` parameter for adding linkable heading anchors to Markdown content ([#15722](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15722), [#13913](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13913)).
- 💻 You can now launch Streamlit apps directly with `python app.py` or `uv run app.py` using the new `App.run()` entry point — no more `streamlit run` required ([#15563](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15563), [#9450](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9450), [#11420](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11420)).

Fragments can update any part of your app — including elements created before the fragment — without triggering a full rerun ([#15623](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15623), [#15620](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15620), [#10481](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10481)).
- 📎 [`st.chat_input`](/develop/api-reference/chat/st.chat_input) now supports pasting files directly into the input field ([#15558](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15558), [#10307](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10307)).

candidates.title: Call arguments don't propogate to st.fragment correctly starting with v1.37
candidates.text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch the provides Streamlit app with Streamlit v1.36
2. You will observe that on the 2nd and later pages the UI responds appropriately in each fragment.
3. Now instead launch it with Streamlit v1.37.1
4. Now, when toggling and 2nd and later pages, the "offset" is incorrectly populated in the fragment, and state from the first page is displayed and affected.
